rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mockery of Muhammad's poverty distressed him; God recalls earlier favors and promises worldly relief, with the fā linking that promise to his distress.
rows.anchor: لا يحزنك ما يقول وما أنت فيه من القلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God created one hardship between two eases, so one hardship cannot overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: خلقت عسرا واحدا بين يسرين ، فلن يغلب عسر يسرين

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: Muqātil reports that the Prophet said one hardship will not overcome two eases and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: عن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قال :  " لن يغلب عسر يسرين "

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj take definite al-ʿusr as generic and thus one hardship in both clauses, while the indefinite yusr denotes two distinct eases.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : العسر مذكور بالألف واللام

rows.speaker: الجرجاني
rows.claim: Al-Jurjānī rejects that grammatical inference: repeating a phrase about one knight and a sword does not entail two swords.
rows.anchor: وزيف الجرجاني هذا وقال : إذا قال الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second clause may repeat the first to establish its meaning firmly, as the repeated warning in 77:15 does.
rows.anchor: ويكون الغرض تقرير معناها في النفوس وتمكينها في القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the two eases are worldly success in opening lands and the afterlife's reward in Paradise, as in the two good outcomes of 9:52.
rows.anchor: يسر الدنيا وهو ما تيسر من استفتاح البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form of yusr magnifies it: the promise is of an immense, remarkable ease.
rows.anchor: ما معنى التنكير في اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although hardship and ease are opposites, ease follows hardship after a short interval so certainly that it is treated as accompanying it.
rows.anchor: لما كان وقوع اليسر بعد العسر بزمان قليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling past favors and promising future ones, God urges gratitude and strenuous worship: when one task ends, undertake worship.
rows.anchor: لا جرم بعثه على الشكر والاجتهاد في العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this command, inṣab means exert yourself or toil; the verb is used as naṣiba yanṣabu.
rows.anchor: أي فاتعب يقال : نصب ينصب

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: After completing the obligatory prayer, exert yourself in supplication to God and ask Him, and He will grant your request.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والضحاك ومقاتل : إذا فرغت من الصلاة المكتوبة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says to supplicate for worldly and afterlife needs after finishing the tashahhud.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي : إذا فرغت من التشهد فادع لدنياك وآخرتك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the instruction as turning from worldly business to exertion in prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : إذا فرغت من أمر دنياك فانصب وصل

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh says that after the obligatory duties one should devote oneself to the night vigil.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله : إذا فرغت من الفرائض فانصب في قيام الليل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that after a military expedition one should strive in worship.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : إذا فرغت من الغزو فاجتهد في العبادة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة
rows.claim: ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭalḥa says that when healthy, one should turn free time into exertion in worship.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة : إذا كنت صحيحا فانصب

rows.speaker: شريح
rows.claim: Shurayḥ saw two men wrestling and remarked that an idle person was not commanded to do that; he invoked the verse's call to exert oneself.
rows.anchor: أن شريحا مر برجلين يتصارعان ، فقال : الفارغ ما أمر بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general instruction is to follow one act of worship with another and leave no time empty of worship.
rows.anchor: أن يواصل بين بعض العبادات وبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is to direct one's desire exclusively to God, ask only His favor, and rely on Him.
rows.anchor: اجعل رغبتك إليه خصوصا ولا تسأل إلا فضله متوكلا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is to seek from God all religious and worldly needs, including victory over enemies.
rows.anchor: ارغب في سائر ما نلتمسه دينا ودنيا ونصرة على الأعداء إلى ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading, farghab, makes the command mean to encourage people to seek what God has.
rows.anchor: وقرئ فرغب أي رغب الناس إلى طلب ما عنده

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī calls this one of the Qur'an's hardest verses in structure and interpretation, saying major scholars struggled with it.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي في كتاب البسيط : هذه الآية من أصعب ما في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent problem is that 98:1 seems to say they left disbelief when the Messenger came, while 98:4 says the People of Scripture divided only after the proof arrived.
rows.anchor: لم يكن الذين كفروا منفكين حتى تأتيهم البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preferring al-Kashshāf's solution, al-Rāzī reads the first clause as the unbelievers' claim that they would not leave their religions until the promised Prophet, Muhammad, came; the next clause reports that his coming instead divided them from truth.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الكفار من الفريقين أهل الكتاب وعبدة الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor sinner analogy shows how a preacher can quote someone's earlier condition as a rebuke: he claimed he would reform when wealthy, then grew more sinful after gaining wealth.
rows.anchor: أن يقول الفقير الفاسق لمن يعظه : لست أمتنع مما أنا فيه

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī construes the clause as saying they would not leave disbelief even if the proof came; al-Rāzī rejects this because hatta does not mean 'even if' in Arabic.
rows.anchor: ذكره القاضي إلا أن تفسير لفظة حتى بهذا ليس من اللغة في شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed reading takes munfakkīn as continuing to praise and mention Muhammad's virtues until the proof came; after his arrival they split and spoke badly of him.
rows.anchor: على الكفر بل على كونهم منفكين عن ذكر محمد بالمناقب والفضائل

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArafa says the wording uses the present form but has past meaning, until the proof came, as in 2:102.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عرفة : أي حتى أتتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise-then-rejection reading parallels 2:89, where people previously sought victory through revelation but rejected what they recognized when it came.
rows.anchor: وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī explicitly selects the first explanation: the clause reports what the unbelievers claimed, whereas the following clause reports what actually happened.
rows.anchor: لم يكن الذين كفروا منفكين } عن كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth solution says the collective group did not leave disbelief before the Messenger, but afterward it changed because some believed and others persisted in disbelief.
rows.anchor: حكم على الكفار أنهم ما كانوا منفكين عن كفرهم إلى وقت مجيء الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth solution says they had been certain of their inherited religions before Muhammad, but his coming unsettled them into doubt and confusion; munfakkīn suggests separation from certainty.
rows.anchor: كانوا قبل مبعث الرسول منفكين عن التردد في كفرهم بل كانوا جازمين به معتقدين حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are two groups: People of Scripture, Jews and Christians who introduced unbelief into their religion, and polytheists who had no scripture.
rows.anchor: الكفار كانوا جنسين ( أحدهما ) : أهل الكتاب كفرق اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One solution to the apparent partitive sense of min is to read it as explanatory, as in the command to shun the abomination of idols in 22:30.
rows.anchor: كلمة من ههنا ليست للتبعيض بل للتبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, min identifies the two sources of those who disbelieved in Muhammad: some were People of Scripture and some polytheists.
rows.anchor: أن الذين كفروا بمحمد عليه الصلاة والسلام ، بعضهم من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis treats al-mushrikīn as a second descriptor of the People of Scripture: Christians are trinitarian and most Jews anthropomorphists, both forms of shirk.
rows.anchor: وصفا لأهل الكتاب ، وذلك لأن النصارى مثلثة واليهود عامتهم مشبهة

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars include the Magians among the People of Scripture, citing the Prophetic instruction to treat them by the rules applied to that community.
rows.anchor: ذكر بعض العلماء أنهم داخلون في أهل الكتاب لقوله عليه السلام : «سنوليهم سنة أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: Others exclude the Magians, arguing that the verse concerns the Arab communities and that 6:156 identifies only Jews and Christians as the two earlier scriptural groups.
rows.anchor: وأنكره الآخرون قال : لأنه تعالى إنما ذكر من الكفار من كان في بلاد العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although conjunction does not establish order, the People of Scripture are placed first because the sura is Medinan, they knew scripture and were more culpable for rejecting Muhammad, others followed them, and they held higher status.
rows.anchor: أن السورة مدنية فكأن أهل الكتاب هم المقصودون بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them People of Scripture rather than naming Jews and Christians can honor them by their learning, or highlight that their learning makes their unbelief more blameworthy and punishable.
rows.anchor: يدل على كونهم علماء ، وذلك يقتضي إما مزيد تعظيم

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Some jurists infer from naming both groups under 'those who disbelieved' that unbelief is one community, so a polytheist may inherit from a Jew and vice versa.
rows.anchor: فمن ذلك قال العلماء : الكفر كله ملة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others take the coordination to distinguish the groups: a protected non-Muslim is not a polytheist, supported by a Prophetic statement about their women and slaughtered food.
rows.anchor: الذمي ليس بمشرك ، وقال عليه السلام : «غيرنا كحي نسائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of learned People of Scripture warns Muslims not to be impressed by scholars: people of the Qur'an can repeat the failings of earlier religious communities.
rows.anchor: نبه بذكر أهل الكتاب أنه لا يجوز الاغترار بأهل العلم إذ قد حدث في أهل القرآن مثل ما حدث

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl derives infikāk from opening or loosening: unsealing a book, releasing a pledge or captive, or separating something joined, like a bone from its joint.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : الانفكاك هو انفراج الشيء عن الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image means they clung tightly to their religion and would not detach from it until the clear proof arrived.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن انفكاك الشيء عن الشيء هو أن يزيله بعد التحامه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa, a receptacle or surface for written material.
rows.anchor: الصحف جمع صحيفة وهي ظرف للمكتوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of purified is that the scriptures are free of falsehood, as 41:42 says and 80:14 describes them as elevated and purified.
rows.anchor: لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Qur'an is purified from blameworthy mention and is instead praised in the finest terms.
rows.anchor: مطهرة عن الذكر القبيح فإن القرآن يذكر بأحسن الذكر ويثني عليه أحسن الثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that the pages ought to be touched only by the ritually pure, as stated in 56:78–79.
rows.anchor: ينبغي أن لا يمسها إلا المطهرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though grammatically an adjective of the pages, purified really describes the Qur'an contained in them.
rows.anchor: وإن جرت نعتا للصحف في الظاهر فهي نعت لما في الصحف وهو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī refers readers to his earlier discussion of al-ʿaṣf in 55:12, 'grain with husk and fragrant plants.'
rows.anchor: ذكرناها في قوله : { والحب ذو العصف }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of al-ʿaṣf is crop leaves left after harvest, blown about and eaten by livestock.
rows.anchor: أنه ورق الزرع الذي يبقى في الأرض بعد الحصاد وتعصفه الرياح فتأكله المواشي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim takes al-ʿaṣf as straw, citing 55:12: wind scatters it from the grain at winnowing; once eaten it is destroyed and offers no protection or return.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : العصف التبن لقوله : { ذو العصف والريحان }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains al-ʿaṣf as the tips of the crop before its grain head ripens.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : هو أطراف الزرع قبل أن يدرك السنبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is grain whose kernel has been eaten, leaving its husk.
rows.anchor: هو الحب الذي أكل لبه وبقي قشره

rows.speaker: مقاتل وقتادة وعطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The phrase can mean crops eaten by animals, excreted as dung, then dried and scattered; the army's severed limbs are likened to the dung's disintegration, expressed euphemistically in Qur'anic diction, as in 5:75.
rows.anchor: كانا يأكلان الطعام } وهو قول مقاتل ، وقتادة وعطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second possibility under 'eaten' is crop leaves damaged by worms.
rows.anchor: أن يكون التشبيه واقعا بورق الزرع إذا وقع فيه الآكال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the phrase as crop whose grain has been eaten and whose straw remains; 'eaten' attaches to the crop by understood ellipsis, as when 'beautiful' means beautiful-faced.
rows.anchor: لأن هذا المعنى معلوم وهذا قول الحسن

rows.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take maʾkūl to mean edible or fit to be eaten: the people were like straw livestock consume.
rows.anchor: والمعنى جعلهم كتبن تأكله الدواب وهو قول عكرمة والضحاك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some argued that al-Ḥajjāj destroyed the Kaaba without a similar event, and thus the Elephant incident either did not occur as described or had another motive than honoring the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : إن الحجاج خرب الكعبة ، ولم يحدث شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that the Elephant event was an irhāṣ, a portent needed before Muhammad's advent; after his prophethood was established by decisive proofs, no such sign was needed.
rows.anchor: وقع إرهاصا لأمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، والإرهاص إنما يحتاج إليه قبل قدومه
